other_failure_modes.name: Model Reference Overwrite Bug
other_failure_modes.description: The agent assigns `best_model = model` inside a cross-validation loop where `model` is instantiated outside the loop. Because `best_model` only stores a reference to the `model` object, subsequent `model.fit()` calls overwrite it in-place. As a result, `best_model` will always be the model trained on the final fold, not the fold with the best validation score.

other_failure_modes.name: Unclipped predictions in RMSLE calculation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent calculates RMSLE using `np.log(y_pred_fold + 1)` without clipping predictions. Since the model optimizes MSE and can output negative values, any prediction <= -1 will result in a NaN value from the logarithm, potentially causing runtime warnings and breaking the validation loop.

other_failure_modes.name: Optimizing MSE for RMSLE evaluation
other_failure_modes.description: The task metric is RMSLE, but the model is trained using the default MSE objective on the raw target. The standard practice to optimize for RMSLE is to apply a logarithmic transformation (e.g., `np.log1p`) to the target before training, and then exponentiate (`np.expm1`) the predictions.

summary: The agent provides a basic LightGBM solution with date-based feature engineering but makes several critical errors. It improperly uses random shuffling for time-series cross-validation (look-ahead bias) and contains a serious reference assignment bug that overwrites the best model during the CV loop. Additionally, it computes RMSLE unsafely without clipping negative predictions and trains on the raw target instead of log-transforming it to align with the evaluation metric.
